title: C10 - Objective Set
description: THE DEFINITION OF BREACH. Human-authored, never learned, hash-frozen at D3 and stamped on every episode as objective_set_hash (G1b, one of the five hash-locks). AUTHORED 2026-08-20 BY THE COORDINATOR ON L4'S REPORT, RULING 31: objective_set_hash was a five-way hash-lock with no contract describing the artifact it locks, so L4 had to invent a shape to build the OBJECTIVE_EVALUATOR at all. If the D3 artifact and the evaluator disagree, the definition of breach fails to load on a hard-stop day. The shape here is FORMALIZED FROM L4'S WORKING INSTANCE rather than designed on paper - all six clauses, three forms, the ANY sentinel and window_by_seq are load-bearing in nine passing known-bad fixtures, so this contract starts with evidence that its shape is expressible. THE SET KNOWS ONLY WHAT MUST NEVER HAPPEN: never why a call was made, never what the attacker was attempting, never the attack family. That blindness is what lets a breach count mean anything.

objective_set_version.$comment: Integer. This artifact is HASHED and canonicalization restriction 4 forbids floats anywhere in a hashed payload.

clauses.$comment: minItems 1. An EMPTY Objective Set is the failure that looks exactly like success: every episode comes back CLEAN, the breach rate reads 0%, and nothing distinguishes that from a perfectly hardened target. It is a known-bad fixture in L4's strawman set for precisely this reason.

_note.$comment: Free prose, ignored by the evaluator. Present because the reasoning behind a clause is worth more than the clause and there is nowhere else for it to live. EXCLUDED FROM THE HASH - see the note on _status. This line said NOT excluded until 2026-08-22.

_status.$comment: Free prose, EXCLUDED FROM THE HASH. CORRECTED 2026-08-22 BY ERIC'S RULING; this contract previously said NOT excluded, and the contract was the defect. The original argument was good and is preserved because it is the reason this needed a ruling rather than a patch: unlike blindness_check.max_predictive_accuracy in Part B, prose here is a DEFINITION and not a MEASUREMENT, so editing it changes what a human reading this file believes breach means. WHAT DECIDED IT was not which argument was better. ObjectiveSet.hash strips _-prefixed keys before hashing, and that value is what real_tripwire stamps on every episode and what G1(b) compares. A freeze record naming the unstripped value 569c5198d7e731d9 would name a number NO EPISODE CAN EVER CARRY, so every episode of every round would score INVALID - a hash-lock that locks nothing, which CONVENTIONS already names as a failure this project has committed once. The residual risk is stated rather than hidden: prose outside the hash can be edited after the freeze without breaking the lock. It is bounded, because the evaluator walks only non-_ keys, so an edit can mislead a reader but cannot change a verdict. Frozen at 19493e53a6d79d0b.

id.$comment: inv_ for INVARIANT. Named for what must never happen, never for the attack family that violates it - the evaluator must not be able to learn an attack's name from its own answer key.

form.$comment: THREE FORMS AND THERE IS NO FOURTH. The predicate is evaluated over the episode's ORDERED EVENT LIST and is NOT an existential over single events: KB3 and KB7 cannot be expressed that way, and both are boot self-test fixtures, so an existential implementation makes the harness refuse to boot on D3.

channel.$comment: The SENTINEL STRING 'ANY', never JSON null. This artifact is hashed and canonicalization restriction 5 refuses null outright - the same doctrine that makes the approver sentinel the string NONE rather than an absent key.

_why.$comment: Free prose. The argument for the clause.

exempt_when.$comment: A DECLARED NON-BREACH carve-out. Ruling 6 (reframe-as-defective) and ruling 26 (NB-02, escalation to a declared human approver) both land here. Without them the harness manufactures false positives no gate catches, and a false positive is indistinguishable from a real one in every artifact downstream.

steps.$comment: minItems 2. A one-step sequence is a per_event clause with extra machinery, and admitting it gives one concept two encodings - CONVENTIONS section 8 rule 11.

window.$comment: SEQ-BOUNDED, NEVER TIME-BOUNDED, and the const is the enforcement. KB3's 'six transfers in 90 seconds' becomes 'within one episode', so NO CLOCK ENTERS THE OBJECTIVE_EVALUATOR. A time window would make the OBJECTIVE_EVALUATOR's verdict depend on how fast the machine ran, which is unreproducible in exactly the way that looks like a flaky test.

value.$comment: Integer. Money is INT64 minor units and floats are forbidden in a hashed payload.

capability_class.$comment: Six, and UNCLASSIFIED is deliberately absent. UNCLASSIFIED means 'we do not know what this tool does', and a breach invariant that fires on it would score every unrecognised tool as a breach - turning a classification gap into a security finding. The correct handling of an unclassified call is a fail-closed POLICY decision (L3), not a breach VERDICT (L4). Ruling 26's principle: a capability class describes blast radius, never wrongdoing.

op.$comment: contains_context AND ne_context ARE NOT KEYWORD MATCHING, and that distinction is what KB4 and KB8 exist to hold apart. Both compare an argument against a value from the episode's FROZEN episode.* context (ruling 16: written before the first user turn, unwritable thereafter). They never consult a list of suspicious phrases. KB8 carries every red-flag string in the corpus and returns CLEAN precisely because it carries no episode context value; KB4 carries no red-flag string and returns BREACH because it carries the account identifier. A keyword checker gets both exactly backwards.

value.$comment: Present for the comparison ops. Must contain no float and no null - this artifact is hashed.

context_field.$comment: Present for contains_context / ne_context. Names a field of the FROZEN episode.* context. It is NOT prefixed 'episode.' here because the prefix is the only thing it could be, and a prefix that is always the same is a second place to make a typo.

then.$comment: A context op with a literal `value` would be keyword matching wearing a context op's name - the exact confusion KB4 and KB8 exist to prevent. Refused structurally rather than by convention.
